summary: Our project, Virtual Space Archaeology Museum, is an interactive educational website developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The main idea behind this project is to explore and showcase the human-made objects, scientific equipment, spacecraft and other materials left behind on the Moon and Mars during various space exploration missions. The website acts as a virtual museum where visitors can discover the history of these objects and understand why they were left behind, when they were placed there and how they became part of space exploration history. We have selected three examples each from the Moon and Mars to provide visitors with interesting information about their missions, purposes, locations and historical importance. Our website aims to make space science and exploration more interesting, informative and accessible through an interactive and visually engaging experience. It also highlights the importance of preserving human achievements in space and helps people understand that even the objects left behind tell valuable stories about humanity's journey beyond Earth.

BEYOND EARTH – The Museum of Forgotten Spacecraft

Team: PIXEL COSMOS

Beyond Earth is a virtual space archaeology museum created to explore the stories of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars.

Space missions do not always bring every piece of equipment back to Earth. From lunar modules and scientific instruments to robotic rovers, these objects remain on other worlds as reminders of human exploration.

Our project brings these forgotten objects into one digital museum. It focuses on three examples from the Moon and three from Mars, explaining their purpose, the missions they belonged to, why they were left behind, and the discoveries associated with them.

Through our website, visitors can discover these objects, understand their historical importance, and explore the stories behind each mission in an engaging and accessible way.

We developed this project as a creative way to connect space exploration with storytelling and digital learning. Instead of presenting space equipment as ordinary mission hardware, we present each object as an important piece of space history.

Our aim is to make space archaeology interesting and understandable for everyone while encouraging curiosity about NASA missions and humanity’s journey beyond Earth.

Project Team: PIXEL COSMOS
